subject: Post-call recap: JSON schema, function-calling & POC success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhang <elaine.zhang@acme-health.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: JSON schema, function-calling & POC success criteria

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the actions we agreed on. I tried to capture goals, pain, current stack, and the success criteria you emphasized. Please correct anything I misunderstood.

Pain points (what you told us)
- Inconsistent output structure from current models: post-processing is expensive and brittle.
- Need strict JSON outputs that map directly to your downstream APIs (claims ingestion, patient-record updates).
- PHI data handling & encryption: must run in your VPC or an isolated deployment with KMS/HSM integration.
- Latency sensitivity for short outputs (interactive agent flows used by clinicians).

Current stack
- Backend: EKS-hosted microservices, internal API gateway, downstream systems behind private network.
- Orchestration: a custom agent that composes prompts and then calls an LLM endpoint, post-processes JSON and calls internal services.
- Security: SOC2 controls, customer-managed KMS, and strict audit logging requirements.

Success criteria you called out
- Deterministic JSON validation: >= 99% strict schema compliance on a 500-prompt eval set.
- Function-calling correctness: typed args must validate 98%+ on the same set.
- Runtime: p50 < 250ms for short, structured responses (under ~200 tokens) during interactive flows.
- Ops: VPC/private deployment with KMS integration and audit logs available to your security team.

Immediate next steps (Redwood)
- Provide an initial JSON schema proposal for your ingestion use case (will attach sample).
- Outline a 4–6 week POC plan (integration + evaluation) with clear metrics and checkpoints.
- Share a pricing ballpark for a POC/private deployment.

Immediate next steps (Acme)
- Share the technical contact for integration (you mentioned Marcus Lin).
- Provide a small representative dataset (500 prompts) and any pre-existing post-processing rules.

Attachments I’ll send with this thread: Acme_sample_schema_v1.json (sample schema we discussed) and evaluation_criteria.xlsx (proposed metrics).

If this aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff next week with Camila (Solutions Eng) and Marcus.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: JSON schema, function-calling & POC success criteria

Ben / team —

Thanks for the thorough recap. A few technical clarifications and a suggested POC scope from SE perspective:

Technical clarifications needed from Acme (please confirm with Marcus)
- Authentication: will integration prefer API keys or mutual TLS / mTLS for the private endpoint?
- Schema evolution: how frequently do your contract schemas change? Do you version them?
- Retry semantics: when your orchestrator receives malformed JSON today, what is the desired fallback behavior?

Suggested POC (high-level, 4-week baseline / can expand to 6)
- Week 0–1: Private endpoint setup (VPC peering + KMS + audit logging), basic auth configured, sample schema deployed.
- Week 1–3: Integration of function-calling mapping (we’ll implement typed args -> internal API calls) and run initial 500-prompt evaluation.
- Week 3–4: Tuning and regression checks, run expanded 2k prompt stress test and report.

Resources from our side
- Camila Reyes (SE) — technical lead for integration and kernel/latency tuning.
- Grace O'Connor (CS) — success metrics and post-POC handoff.

Deliverables
- Sandbox private deployment endpoint and test harness
- JSON schema conformance report (per-prompt pass/fail)
- Function-calling correctness log and sample traces for failed cases

I’ll draft the POC plan and send a calendar invite for a tech kickoff once Marcus is looped in.

Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

From: Elaine Zhang <elaine.zhang@acme-health.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@acme-health.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: JSON schema, function-calling & POC success criteria

Ben / Camila —

Thanks for the summary and the clear plan. Confirming a few items from Acme’s side:

- Technical contact: Marcus Lin (marcus.lin@acme-health.com) will lead the integration work and be the point person.
- Deployment requirement: we require a private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed KMS and HSM support. No hosted shared-tenant endpoints for PHI use cases.
- Security: we’ll complete the attached security questionnaire and expect audit logs sent to our SIEM via syslog or push API.
- Success threshold: our bar for go-live is 99% strict JSON schema compliance and function-call arg validation at 98%+. Lower rates mean additional QA and remediation time.
- Timeline: given internal procurement and legal review, we’re leaning toward a 6-week POC. Budget needs sign-off; can you provide a ballpark POC estimate?

Attachments: Acme_sample_schema_v1.json (simple example of required contract), security_questionnaire_acme.pdf

I’ll upload the representative prompts and a small redacted dataset to the drive link you provide after we sign the NDA.

Regards,

Elaine Zhang
Director of Product, Acme Health
elaine.zhang@acme-health.com
